alt: A mains supply connected to an appliance with a metal case. The live wire, at a high p.d., runs through a fuse and a switch to the working parts; the neutral wire, close to 0 V, completes the circuit; the earth wire, at 0 V, connects to the metal case and carries current only when there is a fault.
caption: Fuse and switch sit in the live wire; the earth wire joins the metal case to the ground.

after: ## Why the switch goes in the live wire
alt: Two circuits with the switch off. With the switch in the live wire, the lamp holder is cut off from the high p.d. and is safe. With the switch in the neutral wire, the lamp goes out but the holder is still connected to the live wire, so it can still give a shock.
caption: Both switch positions turn the lamp off, but only a live-wire switch makes it safe.

alt: A kettle (2.5 kW, 10.9 A), a heater (2.0 kW, 8.7 A) and an iron (1.2 kW, 5.2 A) plugged into one extension lead designed for 13 A on 230 V. The currents add to 24.8 A, so the cable overheats, its insulation can melt and a fire can start.
caption: Each appliance adds its own current; too many on one lead overheats the cable.

alt: A current scale from 0 to 14 A with fuse ratings of 3 A, 5 A and 13 A. A 650 W drill draws 2.8 A, so the 3 A fuse is chosen; a 1.2 kW hair dryer draws 5.2 A, above 5 A, so it needs the 13 A fuse.
caption: Calculate I = P/V, then pick the smallest rating just above it.

alt: A fuse is a thin wire in the live wire that melts when the current exceeds its rating and must be replaced; a trip switch opens when the current exceeds its setting and is reset by hand. A 4.0 kW circuit on 230 V carries 17.4 A, so from 6 A, 20 A and 32 A the 20 A setting is chosen.
caption: Both cut off the live supply when the current is too large; a trip switch can be reset.

alt: A loose live wire touches the metal case of an appliance. A large current flows from the live wire through the case and the earth wire to the ground, the fuse in the live wire melts, the appliance is disconnected and the case is safe to touch.
caption: Fault, large current to earth, fuse melts, live disconnected.

alt: A double-insulated appliance has a plastic, non-conducting case around insulated live parts and only live and neutral wires, with no earth wire. A fuse in the live wire remains to protect the circuit and the cabling.
caption: A non-conducting case cannot become live; the fuse protects the circuit and cabling.
